draft.title: Reproducibility and replicability
card: Replicable
the same person repeats the investigation and gets similar results again.
Reproducible
other people follow the same method and get similar results too.
Results do not need to be identical. Small differences are normal, but the results should be close.
Scientists share their methods in clear detail so others can reproduce the work. Results that others cannot get again are treated with caution.
draft.remember: Replicable: I get it again. Reproducible: others get it too.

a.q: Tom times a pendulum swing three times and gets similar times each run. What can be said about his results?
opts: They are replicable, because he got similar results again
They are reproducible, because he got similar results again
They are replicable, because other people got them
They are reproducible, because the times were identical
a.why: Tom is one person repeating his own test, so the results are replicable. Reproducible needs other people using the same method, and results do not need to be identical.
a.clue: How many people did the testing?

b.q: A Hobart class follows Mei's published method for dissolving sugar in water. Most students get results close to Mei's. What does this show?
opts: Mei's results are reproducible
Mei's results are only replicable
Mei's method must be valid in every case
Mei's results must be exactly correct
b.why: Other people used the same method and got similar results, so the results are reproducible. Agreement between people does not prove the method is valid or the results exact.
b.clue: Who got the matching results this time?

a.best: They are replicable, because he got similar results again

problems.detail: Every wrong option contains an absolute word ('must', 'must', 'only'), and the right option is the only one without one. A test-wise student could pick 'Mei's results are reproducible' without knowing the idea.

check.summary: The card, remember line, question a and both explanations are accurate. In question b, every wrong option uses 'must' or 'only', so the plain right answer stands out and could be picked without knowing the idea.

flags: Question b, wording: Every wrong option contains an absolute word ('must', 'must', 'only'), and the right option is the only one without one. A test-wise student could pick 'Mei's results are reproducible' without knowing the idea.
